text:
raj: Heads up — saw queue_depth spike for us-west-2 GPU pool starting ~09:12 UTC, sustained ~8–12m. Autoscaler didn’t spin up more nodes, pool max=8. Grafana shows batch_size collapse and token latency climb. /d/gpu-pool?orgId=1 :eyes:

infra-bot: [ALERT] GPU_POOL_QUEUE_HIGH - us-west-2-gpu - queue_depth=465, p95_token_latency=320ms - triggered 09:14 UTC

amy: Confirming. I can see the alert, pulling logs. Do we have the promql that fired?

raj: PromQL that alert is based on (from alerts.yaml):
```
expr: max_over_time(queue_length{pool="us-west-2-gpu"}[10m]) > 400
for: 5m
```
One weird thing: batch_size_avg dropped from ~16 to ~4 during the spike.

josie: batch size drop + high queue usually means saturation on a subset of nodes (slow NVLink or a noisy tenant). We should correlate with gpu_util and kv_cache_hit.

amy: Agree. Quick checks:
- grafana panel for per-host gpu_utilization is noisy but not uniformly high.
- network errors spike on host gpu-03 and gpu-07 in logs.

raj: logs excerpt: 
```
[09:13:41] host=gpu-03 ERR network: timeout writing to 10.20.5.7: i/o timeout
[09:13:42] host=gpu-07 WARN batch: dropped 2 requests due to slow prep
```

amy: OK. So autoscaler didn't add nodes because pool_max hit, but we still had room in dedicated-reserve? Not for this pool. Two options: increase pool_max, or tune alerting to open a paging path before hitting hard cap.

josie: For observability improvements, propose:
- Add headroom panel: "effective_headroom" = pool_capacity - max(queue_length + projected_batch_backlog)
- Add histogram of batch_size per model to see tail behaviour
- Track kernel latency per-seq-length to spot regressions

amy: Draft PromQL for headroom suggestion: 
```
pool_capacity{pool="us-west-2-gpu"} - increase(max_over_time(queue_length{pool="us-west-2-gpu"}[5m]), 0)
```
Not perfect; we need a projection based on current batch_size and avg_token_rate.

raj: Also we should tune the alert rule: instead of raw queue_length > 400, use an SLO-aware rule: if queue_length > threshold AND p95_token_latency > SLO_latency AND batch_size_avg < expected, then page. That reduces noise and targets capacity-induced regressions.

sre-oncall: @amy @josie can you propose a new alert rule and a minimal dashboard tweak we can ship today? Oncall window ends at 11:00 UTC.

amy: Will do. Plan:
1) Update a Grafana panel to show per-host queue_length + gpu_utilization + network_err_rate (single-row panel).
2) Create a small dashboard panel for batch_size histogram and p95_token_latency by model.
3) Update alert rule to:
```
expr: (
  max_over_time(queue_length{pool="us-west-2-gpu"}[10m]) > 300
) and (
  max_over_time(p95_token_latency{pool="us-west-2-gpu"}[10m]) > 200
) and (
  avg_over_time(batch_size{pool="us-west-2-gpu"}[10m]) < 8
)
for: 3m
```
This will page infra if queue + latency + batch collapse coincide.

josie: Also add a 'pool headroom' recording rule so dashboards can compute projections cheaply. Something like: 
```
record: pool:effective_headroom:rate5m
expr: pool_capacity{pool="us-west-2-gpu"} - sum(rate(requests_in_flight[5m])) by (pool)
```
Then use that on panels and for autoscaler signals.

raj: Sounds good. Two follow-ups: scale policy review (we probably need burst to dedicated-reserve) and add runbook note: when headroom < 0 and network_err_rate > 5% then consider rack-level remediation.

amy: I'll open a PR for dashboard + alert rule changes, assign to @josie for review. I'll also add a temporary sprint ticket to bump pool_max to 10 if we see repeated pages this week.

infra-bot: Created incident INC-2024-0540 for "us-west-2 GPU pooled saturation" and linked to thread.

raj: Thanks. Quick wins: tune alerting to reduce noise, add headroom recording rules, and add per-host network_err_rate to the pool overview. Longer: autoscaler policy + reserve capacity changes.

sre-oncall: 👍 prioritize the alert rule PR and tag me for rollback instructions. If pages are noisy, we should mute until PR lands.

amy: Will send PR in ~30m. I'll paste the dashboard JSON and the proposed recording rule there.

raj: Great — please ping if you need a rollback key or quick test data.

(reacts: raj :thumbsup:, amy :rocket:)
